scoring_note: 45 objective points (1 each; item 11 counts as 5) + 20 production points (Writing 2 tasks, Speaking 2 tasks, rubric 0-5 each), converted to a weighted percentage. Bands: 0-39 emerging, 40-59 developing, 60-79 consolidating, 80-100 B1 achieved.

items.stem: What time does the heritage tour start?
items.audio_text: Good afternoon. Could you tell me what time the heritage walking tour starts tomorrow? — Of course. It begins at nine fifteen from the main square.

items.stem: How much is the reef tour per person?
items.audio_text: The guided reef tour costs one hundred and twenty thousand pesos per person, life jacket included.

items.stem: Where is breakfast served?
items.audio_text: Breakfast is served on the terrace from seven, and the rooms are cleaned every morning.
items.competency: M-II · 2.1 · voz pasiva en presente (servicios) · listening

items.stem: Where is the gala dinner going to be held?
items.audio_text: Next Friday the gala dinner is going to be held at the old customs house, not at the beach club.

items.stem: What must visitors do on the boat?
items.audio_text: All visitors must wear a life jacket on the boat; you ought to protect the reef by staying on the marked route.

items.stem: How does the host respond to the complaint?
items.audio_text: — I’m really disappointed; the noise from the building work is frustrating. — I completely understand, and I’m sorry. I see your point; however, the work stops at six.

items.stem: Why is the host apologizing?

options.label: A
options.text: because they have moved the event

items.audio_text: — I’m sorry, we have moved the gala dinner to the plaza because of a new local regulation. It’s going to start at eight instead.
items.competency: M-I · 1.4 · presente perfecto + disculpa profesional · listening

items.stem: What does the gallery offer the customer?

options.label: A
options.text: an exchange or a store credit

items.audio_text: — This sculpture arrived damaged. Could I get a refund? — I’m very sorry. According to our policy we can offer you an exchange or a store credit.
items.competency: M-III · 3.1 · devoluciones/situaciones inusuales + modales para ofrecer · listening

items.stem: What does Elena recommend?

options.label: A
options.text: the night market and the concert

items.audio_text: — We have one free evening in town. — I recommend visiting the night market, and you should book the candlelight concert.

items.stem: How does the tourist feel?
items.audio_text: — A tourist photographed the ceremony without permission. — He feels embarrassed and regrets it. If you asked the leaders first, you wouldn’t offend anyone.
items.competency: M-III · 3.3 · sentimientos tras un faux pas + 2.º condicional ligero · listening

audios.text: Could you tell me where the museum entrance is, please?
I’m afraid the ocean tour has been canceled because of the weather.
The gala dinner is going to be held at the old customs house.
Breakfast is served in each eco-suite and the reef is protected by law.
May I see your passport? Do you have anything to declare?

passages.reading_B: Welcome to the old town! While the guide was explaining the legend of the lighthouse, which has warned sailors for two hundred years, a sudden storm began, so we moved indoors. The colonial houses are protected by the community, and the coral reef is now managed by local families. Tomorrow the sunrise boat trip is going to leave at six, although it will be a little shorter than usual because the sea is rough.
passages.reading_C: Guest: Could you tell me (a)___ the gala dinner has been moved? — Host: Yes. It (b)___ now held at the old customs house. I’m sorry; we (c)___ changed the venue. — Guest: I’m a little (d)___, but I understand. — Host: You (e)___ arrive by eight, please.

writing.title: Professional apology email (70-100 words)
writing.prompt: Write a professional apology email to Sarah: the ocean tour has been canceled and the gala dinner has been moved. Explain what has happened (present perfect), what is going to happen now (future forms) and offer a concrete alternative. Close politely.
writing.rubric: formal register · present perfect for what happened · future forms for the new plan · clear alternative + polite apology · cohesion and spelling

writing.title: Balanced report + storytelling (70-100 words)
writing.prompt: Write a balanced report of the day on the coast: what went wrong and how the community solved it. Use past simple and past continuous, connectors (although/however/but) and briefly narrate the positive outcome (resilience / culture of peace). Include at least one comparison (-er than / more ... than).
writing.rubric: balanced contrast (negative to positive) · past simple and continuous · narrative connectors · narration of resilience · one comparison · intelligibility

speaking.title: Read aloud (35-50 s)
speaking.prompt: Read aloud your apology email from Writing Task 1 (or a description of the heritage tour).
speaking.rubric: intelligible pronunciation · courteous intonation · complete and fluent reading

speaking.title: Clarify, compare and recommend (mini-pitch)
speaking.prompt: At reception: handle a complaint, ask for clarification with an indirect question (Could you tell me...?), compare two plan options (as...as / -er than) and finish with a personalised recommendation using a relative clause (the tour which... / a guide who...).
speaking.rubric: clarifies with an indirect question · compares two options · recommends with a relative clause · intelligibility
